items.title: Phantom URL
items.teaser: A phantom URL is a web address an AI presents as a source that does not exist — fabricated at answer time, plausible in structure, resolving to nothing. When the fabricated address carries a brand's domain, the brand inherits the dead end.

items.title: Negated Mention
items.teaser: A negated mention is an AI answer that names a brand in order to advise against it, exclude it, or mark what it lacks. Counting metrics record it as visibility; commercially it works in the opposite direction.

items.title: Brand Rank
items.teaser: Brand Rank is the position a brand occupies when an AI answer lists options. Being named first and being named last are different commercial events that binary presence metrics record identically. Top-3 presence is the operative shortlist threshold.

items.title: Mention Intensity
items.teaser: Mention Intensity measures how much of an AI answer is built around a brand — how often and how substantially it is named within a single response. It is the depth dimension that binary presence metrics flatten.

items.title: Counterfactual
items.teaser: The counterfactual is what would have happened without the intervention. Every claim of marketing effect is a comparison against a counterfactual, whether the person making the claim states one or not.

items.title: Difference-in-Differences
items.teaser: Difference-in-Differences (DiD) measures an effect by comparing the change in a treated group to the change in an untreated group over the same window — subtracting market drift from measured effect.

items.title: Control Group
items.teaser: A control group is the set of units deliberately left untreated so that the counterfactual becomes observable. Its quality, not its existence, decides what the measurement is worth.

items.title: Semantic Anchoring
items.teaser: How deeply a brand is embedded in an AI model's trained knowledge — as opposed to appearing because a document was retrieved. High Mention Rate does not imply anchoring.

items.title: The Invisible Shortlist
items.teaser: More than half of B2B buyers now start vendor research with an AI — and one in three deals goes to a brand they had no awareness of before the AI named it.

items.title: Content Architecture for LLM Authority
items.teaser: Four episodes diagnosed the new reality of AI search. The fifth turns to construction: how to architect content so LLMs treat your brand as a primary source.

items.title: Lead Scoring
items.teaser: Its failure mode is almost never the algorithm — it's the quality of the firmographic data the algorithm is fed.

items.title: MQL — Marketing Qualified Lead
items.teaser: The reliability of the MQL signal depends directly on the quality of the data the scoring system operates on.

items.title: SQL — Sales Qualified Lead
items.teaser: The MQL-to-SQL handoff rate is the sharpest diagnostic signal for the scoring system upstream.

items.title: Touchpoints
items.teaser: In B2B, the path from first contact to a committed decision runs through a sequence of interactions — and each one leaves a trace.

items.title: How to Measure What You Can't See
items.teaser: GEO metrics for the B2B practitioner: when buyers research through ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini before visiting your site, standard analytics are blind.

items.title: The Invisible Buyer Journey
items.teaser: Your prospect compared you to three competitors and read six LLM summaries before ever visiting your site. You saw none of it.

items.title: Why Your Analytics Stack Is Measuring the Wrong Layer
items.teaser: Keywords, rankings and clicks tell you where you appeared — not what the market actually heard.

items.title: The Two-Year Window and Why Most Teams Will Miss It
items.teaser: A 12–24 month lead in semantic intelligence doesn't give a proportional advantage — it compounds into structural market position.

items.title: AI Overviews vs AI Mode
items.teaser: Two distinct Google surfaces with similar answers but largely different cited sources — they must be measured separately.

items.title: Attribution
items.teaser: The discipline of estimating how marketing contacts and channels contribute to pipeline and revenue.

items.title: Platform Divergence
items.teaser: A brand can be prominently visible on one AI platform and absent from another. Single-platform measurement doesn't represent the full picture.

items.title: Hallucination — Brand Risk
items.teaser: A brand with high AI visibility but high hallucination rate is being introduced incorrectly at the most influential moment in the buyer journey.

items.title: Generative Engine Optimization
items.teaser: The practice of improving how a brand is surfaced, cited, and recommended inside AI-generated answers — not in the ten blue links.

items.title: Zero-Click Search
items.teaser: For brands, the question is not only how many clicks fell off, but what the brand says at the moment the answer is served.
